title: perf(security): batch explain runs its object-level pass once, not once per record
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-steve"} -->
_Requested by **Steve** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9?thread=cmsg_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9JQZNr4uFk61WSUkkmYuxEG)_
Fixes #29112

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：批量权限解释（`security/explain` 带 `recordIds`）不再每条记录跑一遍完整解释；调用者校验、被解释用户的上下文和对象级九层只算一次，每条记录只跑记录级判断。
- 为什么改：列表页一行一个菜单，31 行的页要等两次各约 3 秒；本地 50 条 update 批量的数据库查询从 505 次降到 231 次，CPU 从约 284 ms 降到约 147 ms。
- 风险与回滚：答案不变（44 例一致性测试逐条比对批量与单条，覆盖 4 种询问者 × 5 个动作 × 2 个对象的混合记录集）；回滚即还原这一个 PR。
- 先看：`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-engine.ts`（`explainRecordsForAsker` 与拆出的对象级/记录级两段）、`security-plugin-explain-access.ts`（`depsFor`）、`packages/rest/src/security-routes.ts`（把整批交给服务，旧服务退回逐条）。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security exec vitest run src/explain-batch-parity.test.ts`，预期 44 例全绿。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地；staging 上 `Server-Timing runtime ≤ 500 ms` 需发版后由 cloud 侧复测（见 Acceptance notes）。

## What changes

- **Explain engine** (`explain-engine.ts`). `explainOnce` is split, with no change in what it computes, into the object-level pass (`explainObjectPass`: the nine layers and the facts the record pass reads), the record pass (`explainRecordOnPass`) and the decision builder (`decisionOf`). A singular explanation runs them in the same order on the same values as before. A new module export, `explainRecordsForAsker`, runs the object-level pass once and then the record pass per distinct id, each over its own copy of the pass's layers and with the per-explanation read memos `explainAccessForAsker` sets up for one explanation set up afresh. The object-level answer is taken before any record pass runs. The sharing service's read filter (a question about the principal and the object, never a record) is asked once per batch.
- **Security service** (`security-plugin-explain-access.ts`). The deps bag is now built per record (`depsFor(rid)`); only its record-grained members read `rid`. `request.recordIds` is honoured: the caller's admission and the explained context are settled once and the engine's batch entry answers. `recordId` beside `recordIds` is refused, as the wire schema refuses it. The published `SecurityPlugin#explainAccessForCaller` signature is unchanged.
- **REST door** (`security-routes.ts`). The batch is handed to the service in one call. An answer with `records` of the batch's length is relayed, a position with no verdict failing closed as before. A service that predates this answers the object-level decision with no `records`, and the door then asks each id singularly, as it always did.

## Why

The batch form ran `svc.explain` once per id, serially, and each call redid the explained principal's context (its grant rows read again), its person row and the whole object-level pass. On the rig below that was 10 queries per id; it is now about 4.5, all of them the record's own questions.

## Tests

- New `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-batch-parity.test.ts` (44 cases, real `SecurityPlugin`, `SharingService` and sharing middleware over ObjectQL and better-sqlite3, asked through the registered `security` service):
  - AGREEMENT, 40 cases: 4 askers (the member itself as a human, an administrator who reads every row, an administrator held to the member's read policy, the system) × 5 verbs (read, export, update, delete, transfer) × 2 objects (a `private` object behind sharing with an own-row, a shared row, an unshared row, an RLS-locked row, a missing id and duplicates; a `public_read_write` object with an app-authored read policy hiding a row). The member's grant carries a `when`-conditioned field entry and a `unit` read depth with no hierarchy resolver mounted. Each case asserts the batch minus `records` equals the object-level explanation, and `records` equals the singular `record` verdicts in order.
  - The mixed set is mixed (visible, shared, excluded, rls-locked, missing all occur); `recordId` beside `recordIds` is refused.
  - ONE OBJECT-LEVEL PASS, 2 cases: a batch reads the principal's grant rows and person row exactly as often as one singular explanation does.
- `packages/rest/src/security-routes.test.ts`: three new cases (a batch-capable service is called once with the whole batch and its records are relayed; batch-capable AGREEMENT through the real handler; a verdict-less position fails closed).
- **Forced test edits**, both because the service now receives the batch:
  - `security-routes.test.ts`, "answers records[i] for recordIds[i]": the first service call now carries `recordIds` (the fallback calls still carry none). Was: no call carries `recordIds`.
  - `security-explain-envelope.test.ts`, the "batch — POST recordIds, refused by the object-level pass" row: the request the service receives now carries `recordIds`.

## Acceptance notes

- **Card item 1, local half.** On the rig below (50 rows, a human caller explaining itself, `update`): a singular explanation costs about 5 ms CPU; the 50-id batch costs about 147 ms CPU where the per-id loop cost about 284 ms (243 ms on `main`'s own sources). The per-id margin is about 2.9 ms (card bound: 10 ms, met). The "3× a single" arm is NOT met: about 4.5 per-record queries per id remain (the caller's by-id read through the read middleware, the system re-read of the row, the sharing gate and the share listing), and they are each record's own questions.
- **Card item 1, staging half, and item 3** are for the cloud side after release. Estimate only, not measured: staging time is query round trips, and per-id queries fell from about 10 to about 4.5, so roughly half of the 3 s. Reaching 500 ms likely needs one of the two options in the report's open questions (batched per-record reads, or bounded concurrency once the per-request context stamps are made concurrency-safe).
- **`record-page-routes.ts`** is unchanged: its update / delete / transfer verdicts are three different operations, so they share no object-level pass, and this change gives them nothing to share.
- **The service contract type.** `ExplainAccessRequest` (`packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts`) does not declare `recordIds`, while the wire schema (`ExplainRequestSchema.recordIds`) and the decision (`ExplainDecisionSchema.records`) do. This PR touches no `packages/spec` file; declaring it there is a follow-up for the maintainer to decide.
- **Concurrency was considered and rejected**: the RLS composition stamps once-per-request state on the context (`__rlsMembershipStaged`, set before its resolution awaits), so concurrent record passes on one context could read a half-staged membership. The record passes stay serial, in first-occurrence order, as the door asked them.

## Verification

Head `fc99ac4f0bef28e0bbc29e536a4d1b9162e73f51`. Taken on the final head after `origin/main` was merged in (merge base `4550091a1`).

<details><summary>Red first on main's sources</summary>

- `explain-batch-parity.test.ts` with `explain-engine.ts` and `security-plugin-explain-access.ts` restored from `fea2dbb7`: `Tests 42 failed | 2 passed (44)` (the service ignored `recordIds`: `expected undefined to deeply equal [ ... ]`). The 2 that pass there are the read-count pins, vacuously: on main the service never sees a batch, so their red evidence is the ablation below.
- REST suites with `security-routes.ts` restored from `fea2dbb7`: `Tests 4 failed | 48 passed (52)`.
</details>

<details><summary>Ablations (scripts/ablation-replace.mjs, restored blob == HEAD each time)</summary>

- Engine: the object-level pass run once per record inside `explainRecordsForAsker`. Read-count pins red, 2/2: `findOne sys_user` expected 1 received 6 (the member), expected 2 received 6 (the administrator).
- REST: the batch answer ignored (`if (false as boolean)`). Red, 2/25: "hands a batch-capable service the whole batch ONCE", "a position ... fails CLOSED".
</details>

<details><summary>Benchmark readings (shared box, 50 rows, CPU via process.cpuUsage, medians)</summary>

| verb | single CPU | per-id loop CPU | batch CPU | loop queries | batch queries |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| update | 4.97 ms | 284.4 ms (main 243.1) | 147.4 ms | 505 | 231 |
| read | 3.81 ms | 161.3 ms (main 142.5) | 116.1 ms | 430 | 156 |
| delete | 1.95 ms | 175.6 ms (main 185.8) | 135.8 ms | 505 | 231 |

A throwaway script, not committed.
</details>

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security test`: Test Files 239 passed, Tests 5171 passed / 45 skipped.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest test`: Test Files 367 passed, Tests 6966 passed / 332 skipped.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security typecheck`: green. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest typecheck`: green after a test-layer type fix (`fc99ac4f`).
- eslint (repo config, `--no-inline-config`) on the six touched source and test files: exit 0.
</details>

<details><summary>Derived gate list (dispatch-gates --commands)</summary>

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` on `fc99ac4f`: 65 commands. Run reconciliation (`--ran`): 65 derived, 65 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN.

- 62 exited 0 on the first pass.
- `node scripts/check-plugin-teardown-shape.mjs --self-test`: exit 3 (its pinned fixture commit was outside the shallow clone); after fetching that commit, exit 0, "48 cases pass".
- `pnpm check:i18n`: exit 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET, CLI not built); after the closure build it names, exit 0, "OK (10 package(s) — all bundles in sync, no undeclared authoring keys)".
- `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads`: exit 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET (needs every package's dist/, a whole-workspace build). NOT MEASURED locally; CI's Lint and Repo Gates runs it on this PR.
</details>

## Human Minimum

- [x] 1. Schemas start as Zod; `packages/spec` holds no runtime logic.
- [x] 2. Every name I added uses the casing for its kind.
- [x] 3. No formatter ran; `pnpm lint` passes (touched files locally; repo-wide in CI).
- [x] 4. One issue, one branch off an up-to-date `main`, one pull request.
- [x] 5. A change that publishes carries a changeset, and both declaration lines are filled in here and in the changeset.
- [x] 6. `packages/spec` touched: its generated artifacts are regenerated and committed. (Not touched.)
- [x] 7. No hand edits to `content/docs/references/`, `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md` or `content/docs/releases/`.
- [x] 8. Title, body and comments are in English.
- [x] The *Before Submitting* list in CONTRIBUTING.md is done.
